changed: Taken private by Advent in 2023; units renamed Vantor and Lanteris in 2025

name: Speedcast
desc: Satellite communications and IT services company providing connectivity to ships, oil rigs, airlines and remote sites.
markets: Served maritime, energy and airline customers worldwide before its 2020 bankruptcy; now privately held.
rationale: B2B connectivity provider with maritime and energy customers; limited consumer marketing but some hospitality value.
changed: Filed Chapter 11 in 2020, delisted and emerged under creditor ownership

name: Cellnex Nordics
desc: Nordic tower infrastructure business of Cellnex Telecom, owning towers in Sweden, Denmark and Norway for mobile antenna colocation.
markets: Towers in Sweden, Denmark and Norway leased to mobile operators.
rationale: Wholesale tower owner with operator customers and no consumer brand; weak F1 fit.

name: Avia Solutions Group
desc: Dublin-based aviation group, the world's largest ACMI wet lease provider, with airlines, maintenance, flight training and ground handling businesses.
markets: Operates airlines such as Avion Express and Smartlynx plus services in Europe, Asia, Africa and the Americas.
rationale: B2B aviation group with global reach; hospitality could host airline clients, though consumer marketing is limited.

name: Volocopter
desc: German urban air mobility company building all-electric vertical take-off and landing aircraft, including the VoloCity air taxi.
markets: Founded 2011; demonstrations in Europe, Asia and the Middle East; insolvent in 2024 and acquired in 2025.
rationale: Air-taxi technology brand with showcase appeal, but it is a restructured, pre-revenue business.
changed: Filed for insolvency in 2024; acquired by Wanfeng in 2025

name: AVICOPTER
desc: Listed helicopter arm of China's state aerospace group AVIC, designing and making helicopters such as the Z-8, Z-9 and Z-10.
markets: Sells helicopters to Chinese military and civil customers, with some exports; listed in Shanghai.
rationale: State-linked defence and aviation manufacturer with no consumer marketing; F1 sponsorship is unlikely.

name: EnduroSat
desc: Bulgarian space company making small satellites, mainly CubeSats, and selling satellite platforms, components and services.
markets: Sells satellites and platforms to space agencies, companies and universities in Europe and beyond.
rationale: Space technology company with a small budget and B2B customers; modest showcase value.

name: Kymeta
desc: Maker of flat-panel electronically steered satellite antennas that provide mobile connectivity for vehicles, vessels and aircraft.
markets: Sells terminals to military, maritime, aviation and vehicle customers in several regions.
rationale: Connectivity hardware could be shown at events, but customers are mainly governments and fleets; modest fit.

name: TrueNoord
desc: Dublin aircraft leasing and financing company focused on regional aircraft such as ATR and Embraer turboprops and regional jets.
markets: Dublin based; leases regional aircraft to airlines, with customer locations not confirmed.
rationale: B2B lessor with few consumers; hospitality could reach airline customers but marketing culture is limited.

name: Bridger Aerospace
desc: Aerial wildfire management company operating Super Scooper amphibious aircraft and surveillance planes for federal and state agencies.
markets: Serves US federal and state agencies, with some work in Canada and Europe.
rationale: Government-contract firefighting operator with little consumer marketing and no obvious F1 use; weak fit.

name: Loft Orbital
desc: Space infrastructure company leasing capacity on its satellites to customers as a service, with major operations in France.
markets: Based in San Francisco with major operations in France; customers include governments and commercial firms.
rationale: Space technology firm with a small marketing budget; B2B showcase value is modest.

name: Mynaric
desc: Maker of laser communication terminals, such as CONDOR and HAWK, that link satellites to each other and to the ground.
markets: Munich based, with US operations; sells terminals to satellite constellation builders.
rationale: Technology brand with a niche B2B base and uncertain ownership; weak F1 fit.
changed: Went through restructuring in 2025; Rocket Lab agreed to acquire it

name: Avation
desc: Singapore-based aircraft leasing company owning and leasing narrow-body and turboprop aircraft to airlines.
markets: Leases aircraft such as the Airbus A320 family and ATR 72 to airlines in several regions.
rationale: B2B lessor with few consumers; hospitality value for airline clients is modest.

name: Roark Aerospace
desc: London defence technology startup using artificial intelligence in aerospace applications, according to the input; products are not described.
markets: Based in London; products, customers and international plans are not confirmed.
rationale: Unclear startup with no known marketing activity; F1 fit cannot be established and is weak.

name: ZeroAvia
desc: Aerospace company developing hydrogen-electric powertrains for zero-emission aircraft, with a US base in Everett and operations in the UK.
markets: US and UK operations; targets regional aircraft makers and airlines in Europe and North America.
rationale: Sustainable-energy story fits F1's sustainability narrative, but it is pre-revenue with limited budget.

name: Geespace
desc: Shanghai company providing low-Earth-orbit satellite services for high-precision Internet of Things connectivity, part of the Geely technology group.
markets: Shanghai based and linked to Geely; customers are mainly Chinese automotive and IoT users.
rationale: Geely-linked satellite services supplier with automotive customers; modest fit but little standalone brand marketing.

name: ITP Aero
desc: Spanish aeroengine company that designs, makes and maintains engine modules, including turbines and exhaust systems.
markets: Basque-based supplier to engine makers with sites in Spain, the UK, the US and other countries.
rationale: B2B engine supplier with little consumer marketing; engineering showcase potential but modest.

name: Moog
desc: Motion and fluid control company supplying flight controls, actuators and servo valves for aircraft, space, defence, industrial and medical customers.
markets: Sells precision control systems across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific to aerospace, defence and industrial markets.
rationale: Precision motion control is relevant to motorsport engineering, with B2B hospitality value among engineering buyers.

name: XAG
desc: Chinese agricultural technology company making spraying and seeding drones, plus autonomous farm vehicles and robots, for farmers and service providers.
markets: Sells drones to farmers in China and in markets across Asia, Europe, Africa and the Americas.
rationale: Consumer-facing farm technology brand with international growth; F1 gives technology profile, though farmers are not core F1 audiences.

name: Korea Aerospace Industries
desc: South Korea's main aerospace manufacturer, building the T-50 Golden Eagle trainer jet and FA-50 light combat aircraft.
markets: Sells trainers and fighters to South Korea and export customers in Asia, Europe and Latin America.
rationale: Defence-focused manufacturer selling to governments with limited consumer marketing; F1 sponsorship is unlikely.

name: Gilat Satellite Networks
desc: Israeli maker of satellite communications equipment and services, selling VSAT terminals, ground systems and broadband services.
markets: Serves aviation, maritime, defence and telecom customers across several regions.
rationale: B2B satellite equipment supplier; connectivity technology showcase possible but consumer marketing is limited.

name: Electro Optic Systems
desc: Australian defence and space technology company making remote weapon systems, counter-drone and laser defence systems, and space situational awareness tools.
markets: Sells to militaries in the US, Europe and the Middle East, with Australian and US operations.
rationale: Weapons supplier selling to governments with no consumer brand; F1 sponsorship is very unlikely.

name: Flying Whales
desc: French aerospace company developing the LCA60T, a rigid airship for transporting heavy and oversized loads such as wind turbine blades.
markets: Based in Suresnes; operations in France and Canada; no commercial flights yet.
rationale: Heavy-lift airship with a sustainability angle and French base, but pre-revenue with a small budget.

name: Interstellar Technologies
desc: Japanese aerospace company developing small commercial rockets, including the ZERO orbital launcher and MOMO sounding rocket, and satellites.
markets: Based in Taiki, Hokkaido; launches from Japan for Japanese customers.
rationale: Japanese space brand with a modest budget could use Suzuka for showcase, but fit is weak.
